text.p: Daewoo Securities (Hungary) rated the Hungarian hotel chain Danubius a "buy" on Friday, saying the firm's results and developments and the outlooks of the country's tourism industry are encouraging.

"Taking into account the recent developments at the Company and the favourable expectations regarding the growth of tourism to Hungary, in our view Danubius is an attractive share on long-term," said Daewoo analyst Zoltan Varadi in a company update.
Daewoo said that the quality of Danubius' services and its financial stability improved considerably in the past few years.

The company's plans for 1996, including a two percent increase of the occupancy level of its hotels, a 22 percent rise in sales and a nine percent increase of pre-tax profit, are realistic, the analyst added.
"The plans of Danubius seem viable taking into account the last year's developments and the increasing number of business trips and the growing tourism to Hungary in 1996," he said.
Danubius spent 652 million forints on investments and reconstruction in 1995 from its own sources, and the reconstruction and modernisation continued in 1996, Daewoo said.

While the company's strategy to grow through acquisitions and investment in its hotels will entail negative cash-flow in the short term, in the long term the policy can yield an attractive return, Varadi said.
Danubius increased its market share to between 27 and 29 percent recently, with the acquisition of the HungarHotels chain, Daewoo said.

"As a result of the recent developments at the company, Dabubius is able to combine the possibilities in the Hungarian tourism sector with the advantages of spa hotels with their longer-term, higher spending, more regular guests," it added.
Danubius closed at 3,370 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Friday, up 65 forints.
